prose.summary: The aluminium windows meet the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. This results in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED.
prose.classification: The product is classified under HS code 76101000, described as doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is medium, and the code should be confirmed with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and at least 45% value addition (VA). CTSH means each non-originating input must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the product, while VA is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials. The final manufacture check confirms that the last manufacturing step took place in the UAE, and the minimal operations check confirms that the work done goes beyond the simple operations that never give origin on their own. The CTSH check is satisfied because all three non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, and the VA check is satisfied with a build-down of 43.0% against the 40% threshold on an Ex-Works basis.

notes.text: The certificate fee is based on the invoice value in AED according to the UAE e-service schedule, and the fee calculation assumes the invoice value equals the shipment value given.

UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum, but the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims. The certificate does not remove the importer's duty of reasonable care, so the exporter may be asked for production and cost details.
The '+' symbol in the product-specific rule is read as 'and', meaning both tests must pass. The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Fee bands are those of the certificate service (UAE e-service: Certificate of Origin for India; Ministry service pages; Cabinet Resolution 208/2025 fee schedule), charged on the invoice value in AED.
Assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
By interpretation, de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
Minor typing or formatting errors are tolerated; discrepancies in signature or seal are not. A lost certificate can be replaced by a certified true copy.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found). Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
The certificate does not remove the importer's duty of reasonable care, so the UAE exporter may be asked for production and cost details.
The 8-digit code 76101090 you gave is not a line in India's tariff; Mansha matched it on its first 6 digits (761010). 8-digit codes are national and differ between the UAE and India.
